finding.claim: Mass assignment: PUT /me copies the entire request body onto the authenticated user object and persists it, so any user can set privileged fields (e.g. role, isAdmin, id, email verification, tenant/org id) on their own account.
finding.source: req.body (JSON from authenticated client, arbitrary keys)

trace.note: PUT /me handler; only authentication (req.user) is assumed
Object.assign merges all attacker-supplied keys into the server-side user record with no allowlist
updated user returned to the client

finding.guards_checked: No field allowlist or schema validation on this route. Contrast with /me/profile (lines 11-12), which destructures only displayName and bio. No middleware visible in this file filters body keys. Not a decoy: the whole body is merged rather than an allowlisted subset.

verdict.reason: users.js:5 runs Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist, users.js:6 persists it and users.js:7 returns it; users.js is the only file in the directory, so no middleware or schema validation exists, and the allowlisted /me/profile route (users.js:11-12) shows the filtering was skipped on this route.
